resolve_disembargo.note: Reflected-capability resolve/embargo. The one remaining per-direction skip is a reference-library gap, not capnp-zig behavior; recorded as SKIP by tools/e2e_runner.zig (resolveDisembargoSkip). See docs/supported-surface.md Known limitations #4.

zig-client_to_reference-server.reason: pycapnp cannot host the reflecting server (no promise-fulfiller API to return an unresolved capability and resolve it later).

reference-client_to_zig-server.reason: W1 (v0.3.0) made the reflected-loopback return a plain sendResultsTo=caller call with plain .results — consumable by all four reference clients. The earlier go/rust skips (go-capnp could not parse takeFromOtherQuestion; capnp-rpc stalled on it) were removed.

l3_l4_interop.note: Experimental L3/L4 interop lane. C++ is the only runnable L3 runtime proof today. Go is covered by the source-backed `just e2e-l3-go` blocker probe because vendored go-capnp exposes Network3PH names but still TODO/panics on the required runtime 3PH paths.

zig-client_to_reference-server.reason: C++ has the runnable TCP L3 handoff harness. Go is runtime-blocked by TODO 3PH paths checked by `just e2e-l3-go`; Python and Rust adapters currently expose only two-party paths.

reference-client_to_zig-server.reason: The current l3_l4_interop orchestrator is Zig-client-only: vats A/B are capnp-zig and the reference backend hosts vat C.
